title: Mechanistic refinement of non-invasive autonomic neuromodulation for cardiac arrhythmia
text:
The aim of this proposal is to enhance the career development of the candidate through 1) a didactic
Master of Science program in translational research as well as formal neuroscience training and 2)
patient-oriented research in autonomic neuromodulation. A longstanding goal of cardiovascular research
is to characterize the role of the autonomic nervous system in the pathogenesis of cardiac arrhythmias
and technical advances in neuroscience have given rise to powerful new ways to interact with neural
circuits. Application of these new methodologies in the investigation of the cardiac-neural axis and in the
treatment of patients with VT storm may provide critical information regarding the mechanistic
characterization of complex autonomic pathways and help establish the role of a novel method of
neuromodulation.

title: Synaptic changes in the medial prefrontal cortex in the development of compulsive alcohol drinking
text:
The experiments in this project will use an animal model of alcohol self-administration to study maladaptive changes in
synaptic plasticity in specific prefrontal cortical networks that occur in the transition from goal-directed to compulsive
alcohol drinking. Understanding the development of these changes is important as they are likely to contribute to
cognitive deficits and impact the ability of the prefrontal cortex to regulate drug-seeking behavior.

title: Genetic studies of a pleiotropic transmembrane protease: insight from color variation in non-model organisms
text:
Mendelian variation in pigmentation is a rich genetic resource to understand signaling pathways relevant to
human biology and has led to the identification of a novel transmembrane protease, Transmembrane
aminopeptidase Q/Laeverin (Taqpep/LVRN), involved in biology of the placenta, hair, palate, and gut. This
application uses pigmentary variation in animals to discover new genes that interact with Taqpep, and to better
understand Taqpep function by studying knockout mice.

title: Computational and experimental framework for the integrated tissue analysis of spatial metabolomics and transcriptomics datasets
text:
Spatial analysis provides invaluable insights into tissue architecture and plays a crucial role in advancing our
explorations of biological processes and disease mechanisms. Recent advancements have enabled the
technological development of spatial metabolomics and spatial transcriptomics, two powerful methods for
studying gene expression and metabolic activities in the context of tissue architecture. Here we propose to
develop a computational and experimental framework for the joint analysis of spatial transcriptomics and
spatial metabolomics for biological insights into cellular adaptation to drug resistance.

title: Endothelial de novo nucleotide synthesis in atherosclerosis
text:
Endothelial metabolism plays a critical role in regulating endothelial function, and dysregulated endothelial
metabolism leads to the development of various vascular diseases, including atherosclerosis. Our proposed
study aims to uncover previously unrecognized connections between de novo nucleotide synthesis and
endothelial dysfunction within the context of atherosclerosis. The results of our study will provide insights into
how metabolic reprogramming of purine and pyrimidine synthesis in endothelial cells is involved in the
development of atherosclerosis, offering new strategies for its prevention and treatment.

title: Identification of allosteric molecules for DOR-KOR heteromer-mediated peripheral analgesia
text:
The delta opioid receptor (DOR)- kappa opioid receptor (KOR) heteromer expressed in pain-sensing neurons is
a promising target for development of peripherally-restricted analgesic drugs to treat pain. In this project, a
multifaceted and highly collaborative approach to identify small, drug-like molecules that selectively activate the
DOR-KOR heteromer will be done to identify lead molecules for further development as potential pain
therapeutics.

title: Optimizing Agricultural Work Environments through NextGen Human-Robot Interactions: Assessing Safety, Performance, and Psychosocial Reactions to Soft vs. Rigid Robots
text:
Accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic, the world of work is undergoing momentous change with nearly half of
all occupations being ripe for automation within the next two decades. However, technical and psychological
barriers to adoption of Human-Robot Interaction (HRI) remain that threaten the health and safety of workers
operating in collaboration with robotic technology. Our project seeks to demonstrate that HRI with novel soft
growing flexible robots compared to traditional rigid body manipulators will result in greater trust in and openness
to HRI, fewer perceived safety hazards, better safety and task performance, and fewer negative physiological
stress reactions.

title: The Leukocyte RNA Biomarkers in Dystonia
text:
The proposed experiments aim to systematically identify leukocyte RNA biomarkers associated with dystonia,
laying the groundwork for future mechanistic studies. We will also examine the role of the previously identified
biomarker MALAT1 in dystonia pathogenesis. These findings are expected to offer valuable insights for clinicians
and researchers working to improve diagnosis, monitoring, and treatment of the disorder.

title: Machine learning of biomolecular interactions and the human signaling networks they comprise
text:
Signal transduction networks are the information processing engines of the cell, and their dysregulation leads to
many human diseases. Despite their fundamental importance, little is understood about how signaling networks
vary across individuals and human populations, and how this variation interacts with pathogenic mutations to
drive disease. We will develop a research program focused on developing computational tools to predict protein-
ligand interactions in signaling networks and applying them to large-scale genomic datasets to investigate
variability and dysregulation of human cell signaling.

title: The Benefits, Risks, and Long-term Impact of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Children
text:
PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE
The use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) in children for obesity and type 2 diabetes
(T2D) is rapidly increasing due to their clinical benefits and recent FDA approvals. By leveraging real-world data
(RWD) and advanced analytical methodologies, our project aims to develop a robust and generalizable analytical
framework for conducting rigorous causal assessments of the benefits and risks associated with pediatric GLP-
1RA use. Our ultimate goal is to generate high-quality real-world evidence (RWE) that directly informs clinical
decision-making and meaningfully improves long-term outcomes in pediatric populations.

title: Temporal Pattern Perception Mechanisms for Acoustic Communication
text:
Normal speech comprehension and communication are rooted in basic auditory cognitive
processes. Deficits in these processes accompany severe communication disorders (e.g.
auditory processing disorder, dyslexia, specific language impairment, autism), and their
abnormal function can compound the negative impacts of hearing impairments. The proposed
project investigates the neuronal mechanisms of auditory temporal pattern processing using
natural communication signals, with the ultimate goal of understanding the neurobiological basis
of language-relevant abilities and improving treatment of communication processing disorders.

title: Triple-enriched metagenomics for robust resistome analysis
text:
This proposed work is relevant to public health because it develops a novel high-throughput
method for extracting valuable information from metagenomic data, with a focus on critical
antimicrobial resistance genes and the pathogens that harbor them. This contribution is significant
because it will enable improved clinical and public health decisions regarding antibiotic use and
interventions to break transmission of antimicrobial resistant pathogens. The outcomes of the
work therefore support NIH's mission to reduce morbidity and mortality by combating antimicrobial
resistance.

title: Investigating RNA dysregulation in Neurological Disease through study of Pontocerebellar Hypoplasia Type 1b
text:
Pontocerebellar Hypoplasia Type 1b (PCH1b) is a devastating inherited neurological disorder that preferentially
affects specific regions of the brain, the pons and the cerebellum, causing children born with this condition to
have dramatically reduced lifespans. The mutations that cause PCH1b occur in a gene that encodes a critical
component of a molecular machine that is important for the regulation of gene expression. The proposed studies
exploit the fruit fly (Drosophila) as a model system to provide insight into molecular mechanisms underpinning
PCH1b.

title: Remote injury responses after AKI
text: Sterile tissue injury e.g. by ischemia or trauma can induce a systemic inflammatory syndrome with remote organ inflammation and dysfunction. Sterile ischemic acute kidney injury (AKl)-associated worsening of respiratory failure in multiorgan failure patients is common in the Veteran population but not well understood mechanistically, causing high mortality due to lack of therapeutics. The proposed research is relevant to the mission of the Veterans Administration, as it may lead to the development of novel therapeutic options in multiorgan failure and could significantly impact suffering and health care expenditure.

title: Elucidating fungal and bacterial polymicrobial interactions during catheter-associated urinary tract infections
text:
Catheter-associated urinary tract infections (CAUTIs) are one of the most common nosocomial
infections. For a long time, CAUTI were considered to be caused by a single pathogen at the time. However,
recent clinical data have shown that these infections are often polymicrobial. Polymicrobial infections account
for 97% in patients with long-term catheterization. To make matters worse, patients with weakened and
compromised immune systems increase their risk of developing septicemia, leading to organ failure, septic shock
and death. Thus, by trying to understand polymicrobial interactions amongst of some the most prevalent
uropathogens, E. coli, E. faecalis, and C. albicans, we will generate key information for the development of better
prevention and treatment option to improve quality of lives and minimizing casualties.

title: Lineage tradeoffs during injury-accelerated intestinal cell differentiation
text:
These studies will illuminate the mechanisms coordinating cellular flux during Drosophila
intestinal regeneration, when the tissue must balance the demands of urgent repair against
longer-term return to homeostasis. These tradeoffs involve fate and regenerative signals
(Notch-Delta, Hippo/YAP, Myc) and processes (accelerated differentiation, stem cell exhaustion,
injury-induced fate plasticity) that are broadly conserved across metazoans. Our findings will
thus provide a general framework for understanding the orchestration of cell lineage dynamics
during regeneration of organs in many metazoans, including humans.

title: Deciphering the Turnover of Proteome and Phosphoproteome in Alzheimer's Disease
text:
We will investigate how proteome and phosphoproteome turnover is altered in specific brain regions and cell
types during the progression of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). This study will uncover the dynamic regulation of
protein stability in AD and identify phosphorylation-dependent mechanisms that impair the proteostasis network
and contribute to neurodegeneration. Our findings will provide mechanistic insights into how protein degradation
fails in AD and reveal new therapeutic vulnerabilities to restore proteostasis and mitigate disease progression.

title: Exploring conformational and chemical spaces with advanced molecular simulation algorithms
text:
The targets of drug molecules in the human body are not static, they are dynamic and can
respond to drug molecules in ways that are both subtle and overt. This project uses
computational approaches to model the motions of drug receptors in the body, including new
artificial intelligence models that can search for new drugs inside moving receptors. This work
will ultimately improve the efficiency in the discovery of new drugs for a variety of diseases.

title: A dual-layer flat panel x-ray detector based on an engineered amorphous chalcogenide alloy for quantifying coronary artery calcium
text:
The proposed research will apply a novel dual-layer x-ray detector for calcium scoring to enable early detection
and intervention of cardiovascular disease, especially when patients are asymptomatic. Our technology, which
innovatively combines material engineering to tune electro-optical properties of chalcogenide alloys, detector
structure design, and artificial intelligence-guided image processing, brings much-needed quantitative
capabilities to x-ray imaging. This approach will allow accurate quantification of coronary artery calcium from
chest x-rays and will have immense impact on proactive healthcare, improving the clinical outcomes of patients,
and reducing the number of deaths associated with cardiovascular disease.
